title: Kazakh — Latin alphabet (April 2021 version)
authority: Decree No. 569 (26 Oct 2017) as amended by Decree No. 637 (19 Feb 2018); alphabet revision presented Jan 2021, Ŋ→Ñ on 22 Apr 2021
description: Kazakh Cyrillic to the 2021 Latin alphabet (31 letters): Ә→ä, Ғ→ğ, И and Й→i (capital İ), І→ı (capital I), Ң→ñ, Ө→ö, Қ→q, Ұ→ū, Ү→ü, Ш→ş, Ж→j, Х and Һ→h, Ы→y; Russian-only letters Ё Ю Я Ц Ч Щ → io iu ia ts tş ştş, Ъ and Ь dropped.
notes: Status draft: the 2021 alphabet is the official target ('used from 2023'), but the transition deadline is 2031 and Kazakh remains effectively Cyrillic in 2026; no confirmation was found that identity documents use it.
The handling of Ё, Ц, Ч, Щ, Ю, Я (io, ts, tş, ştş, iu, ia) is taken from Wikipedia's comparison table; the research notes flag it as uncertain.
Superseded versions: 2017 apostrophe alphabet (Decree 569: a', g', n' …) and 2018 acute alphabet (Decree 637: Á, Ǵ, Ń, Ó, Ú, Ý for У, I ı for И/Й).

Casing workaround: Python upper-cases i to I, but here capital i must be İ while I is the capital of ı (І). И/Й are emitted as a placeholder (U+0269/U+0196) that post rules turn into i/İ (Ислам → İslam, Ілияс-type І → I).
